known.title: The overlay fallback gives `not applicable` when the contract holds only some of the removed lines
known.summary: writeContractCopy returns `not applicable` when one removed line is missing from the snapshot contract (prepare.mjs:841). Its comment (lines 819-824), SKILL.md line 112, and the test header (review-benchmark.test.mjs:5643) give `not applicable` only to a contract that holds no removed line, and say that every other failure of `git apply` stops `case`. So when the contract holds one removed line, for example the settled-decision sentence of decision 7, and another removed line differs, the run records `not applicable` and measures the variant without its contract change. This is the hidden failure that the round-2 finding reported. The new test (lines 5902-5970) uses only contracts with all or none of the removed lines, so it still passes.

known.title: The self-review test for a project folder with a space does not give the folder to its fixture
known.summary: The test loop at review-benchmark.test.mjs:3963-3965 names the folder `review project`, but it calls `selfReviewAgents(t)` without the folder. So both runs use the folder `project`, and no test has a self-review agent file path with a space. The repair changed SELF_REVIEW_AGENT_FILE and its reader for quoted paths (score.mjs:122-131 and 1724), but a revert of that change passes every test. No caller sets the new `projectFolder` parameter of selfReviewAgents (line 3819).
